What you can get

Finding one

About 1 in 1,250 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Cosmic

The blanket starts at the dorsal midline and spreads down and out from it, one continuous region with no holes in it and no islands off it. It runs from the poll to the croup - the whole length of the neck as well as the barrel, hanging off the crest the way it hangs off the back - and stops above the elbow and stifle, never onto a limb, never onto a hoof. Its lower boundary is a long soft fade rather than a line: there is no edge on this marking anywhere. Inside are stars, thickest near the topline and thinning toward the edge, with a planet or a spiral galaxy on a heavily marked horse. Where the blanket meets the mane or the tail base the colour runs on into the hair, deepening toward the tips.

  1. the blanket, hung from the topline — AXIS × WAVES × PATCHES × AXIS, painted with RAMP
  2. the starfield inside it, densest at the spine — SPECKLE × AXIS × WAVES × PATCHES, painted with TOWARD
  3. a planet or two, with a ring at an angle to it — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with PALETTE
  4. the ring around each planet — RINGS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
  5. the colour carried into the mane and tail — PARTS, painted with RAMP

Wild type

No blanket.

Paints nothing.
